content_groups.group_title: Q1. What are the four components of a joint examination?

blocks.text: Look, feel, move and assess function.

content_groups.group_title: Q2. Why do you examine the normal side first?

blocks.text: To establish a baseline and allow comparison with the affected side.

content_groups.group_title: Q3. What does painful passive movement suggest?

blocks.text: It suggests pathology within the joint, particularly inflammation or infection.

content_groups.group_title: Q4. What does reduced active movement with preserved passive movement suggest?

blocks.text: Muscle weakness, neurological disease or pain-related inhibition rather than primary joint restriction.

content_groups.group_title: Q5. What does Trendelenburg test assess?

blocks.text: Hip abductor function, particularly gluteus medius.

content_groups.group_title: Q6. What causes a positive Trendelenburg test?

blocks.text: Weakness of the hip abductors, which may occur with developmental dysplasia of the hip, hip pathology or superior gluteal nerve dysfunction.

content_groups.group_title: Q7. What are the causes of a limp in a child?

blocks.text: **Trauma, infection, inflammatory disease, malignancy, neurological disease and orthopedic conditions.**
**Q8. What is the most important diagnosis to exclude in an acutely painful swollen joint?**

content_groups.group_title: Q9. Why is septic arthritis an emergency?

blocks.text: Because infection can rapidly destroy the joint and lead to systemic sepsis.

content_groups.group_title: Q10. A child has knee pain. What joint must you examine?

blocks.text: **The hip**, because hip pathology can present as referred knee pain.

content_groups.group_title: Q11. What is a positive Galeazzi test?

blocks.text: A difference in knee height when the hips and knees are flexed, suggesting possible femoral shortening or hip dislocation.

content_groups.group_title: Q12. What does a rib hump on forward bending suggest?
Q13. What is the difference between true and apparent limb shortening?

blocks.text: True shortening is an actual difference in bony limb length, while apparent shortening results from pelvic tilt, hip deformity or other positional factors.
Always assess gait when age appropriate.

content_groups.group_title: 🔑 The 10 things I would absolutely not forget in a pediatric musculoskeletal OSCE

items.text: **Examine the hip in every child with a limp.**
**Hot, swollen, acutely painful joint = exclude septic arthritis urgently.**
**Adapt the examination to the child's age and cooperation.**

blocks.text: If the examiner gives you a **child with a limp**, don't immediately start manipulating the knee.
**“I need to observe the gait and examine the hip, knee, ankle and foot, while considering trauma, infection, inflammation and orthopedic causes.”**
That single approach prevents several common OSCE errors.
